verses.text: So be careful, or one of you may miss the promise of entering God's rest.
We've heard the Good News just as they did. But their message did them no good, because they didn't join what they heard with faith.
But we who have believed do enter that rest. God said, ‘In my anger I swore they would never enter my rest,’ even though his works were finished since the creation of the world.
Somewhere God spoke about the seventh day: ‘God rested on the seventh day from all his work.’
And in this passage he says again, ‘They will never enter my rest.’
Since it remains true that some will enter that rest, and those who first heard the Good News failed to enter because of disobedience,
God set another day—‘Today’—when, long afterward, he spoke through David, as already quoted: ‘Today, if you hear his voice, don't harden your hearts.’
If Joshua had given them rest, God wouldn't have spoken later about another day.
So a Sabbath rest remains for God's people.
Those who enter God's rest also rest from their work, just as God rested from his.
So let's make every effort to enter that rest, so no one will fall by following the same example of disobedience.
God's word is alive and active, sharper than any double-edged sword. It cuts through to divide soul and spirit, joints and marrow, and judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
Nothing in creation is hidden from God. Everything is exposed and laid bare before the eyes of the one to whom we must give an account.
So since we have a great high priest who has gone through the heavens—Jesus, the Son of God—let's hold firmly to what we believe.
We don't have a high priest who can't understand our weaknesses. He was tempted in every way just as we are, but he didn't sin.
So let's approach the throne of grace with confidence, where we'll receive mercy and find grace to help us when we need it.
